label: Fictional sample data
evaluationSummary: Initial evaluation 2024-04 (fictional results): PT evaluation shows reduced balance and endurance for school-distance walking; OT evaluation: Beery VMI standard score 76, fine motor precision below age expectations. Academic screening within the average range. Medical information is on file with the school office; no details are recorded here.
strengths: Sleepy is curious, has strong oral language, reads near grade level and is a persistent problem solver.
needs: Getting around school safely and on time with his walker; handwriting legibility and speed; keyboarding; managing his materials.
parentConcerns: His family wants him to move around school as independently as he safely can and to keep up with written work.
disabilityImpact: Motor limitations affect mobility between school locations, written output and handling materials, which reduces his participation and work completion without supports.

presentLevels.text: Reads 52 words correct per minute on grade 2 passages (near the fall benchmark); comprehension at grade level.
Grade-level number sense; written computation is slow because of handwriting.
Walks school distances with a posterior walker. Classroom to cafeteria takes about 7 minutes with minimal assistance on the ramp.
Copies a sentence with 50% legible letters; types 3 words per minute with hunt-and-peck.
Unpacks and packs his backpack with adult help on 2 of 5 days.

specialFactors.notes: Assistive technology: slant board, pencil grips, adapted paper, keyboard with word prediction; personal walker.

transition.note: Not required: the student is in elementary school (Georgia requires a transition plan by 9th grade entry or age 16).

goals.baseline: Classroom to cafeteria in about 7 minutes with minimal assistance on the ramp.
goals.statement: Using his walker, Sleepy will travel between the classroom, cafeteria and bus loop within 4 minutes with supervision only in 4 of 5 trials.
goals.criteriaForMastery: Within 4 minutes, supervision only, 4 of 5 trials

objectives.statement: Sleepy will go up and down the ramp with stand-by assistance in 4 of 5 trials.
Sleepy will travel classroom to cafeteria within 5 minutes.

goals.baseline: 50% legible letters when copying a sentence.
goals.statement: Using a slant board and adapted paper, Sleepy will copy a sentence with 80% legible letters in 4 of 5 samples.

objectives.statement: Sleepy will form lowercase letters a-m legibly with 80% accuracy.

goals.statement: Sleepy will type 8 words per minute with 90% accuracy using word prediction across 3 consecutive probes.

objectives.statement: Sleepy will type 5 wpm with 90% accuracy.

goals.baseline: Manages backpack with adult help on 2 of 5 days.
goals.statement: Sleepy will unpack and pack his backpack and materials independently on 4 of 5 days for 3 consecutive weeks.

objectives.statement: Sleepy will unpack independently on 4 of 5 days.

services.location: Lift-equipped bus (provided by the resident district)

accommodations.description: Leaves class 3 minutes early for transitions; elevator access
Slant board, pencil grips and adapted paper
Keyboard with word prediction for written work longer than 2 sentences
Scribe or keyboard for written responses; extended time
Adult supervision during hallway transitions and on stairs or ramps

alternateAssessmentReason: Grade 2: no statewide assessment. District benchmarks given with the classroom testing accommodations above.
lreExplanation: Sleepy attends a separate special education school by family choice with a scholarship. He joins all school-wide activities with mobility supports.

esy.notes: Considered; not needed. Home exercise program provided by PT/OT.
